title: Keep every customer
prompt: Show every customer's name and their order id as order_id. Customers with no orders must stay. Replace the ___.
hints: The table that must keep all its rows comes first.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name, o.id AS order_id FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, o.id AS order_id FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;
SELECT c.name, o.id AS order_id FROM orders o LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id;

title: Departments and staff
prompt: Show every department's name as department, and each employee's name as employee. Departments with no staff must stay.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT d.name AS department, e.name AS employee FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT d.name AS department, e.name AS employee FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id;
SELECT d.name AS department, e.name AS employee FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id;

title: Counting with zeros
prompt: Show each customer's name and number of orders, as orders. Customers with no orders must show 0.
hints: COUNT a column from the right table.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
wrongSolutions.why: COUNT(*) counts the empty row as 1

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

title: Every course's enrolments
prompt: Show each course's title and its average grade as average, rounded to 1 decimal. Courses with no grades show NULL.
hints: AVG over no values gives NULL.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT c.title, ROUND(AVG(e.grade), 1) AS average FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.title;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.title, ROUND(AVG(e.grade), 1) AS average FROM courses c JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.title;
SELECT c.title, AVG(e.grade) AS average FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.title;

title: Zero instead of NULL
prompt: Show each product's name and total units sold, as units. Products that never sold must show 0, not NULL.
hints: SUM over nothing is NULL, so use COALESCE.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO products VALUES (10, 'Vase', 'Home', 5.0, 2.0);

solutions: SELECT p.name, COALESCE(SUM(i.quantity), 0) AS units FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.name, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name;
SELECT p.name, COALESCE(SUM(i.quantity), 0) AS units FROM products p JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name;

title: Fix the lost rows
prompt: This should show every employee's name and department as department, including employees with no department, but one is missing. Fix it.
hints: An inner join drops unmatched rows.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id;
SELECT e.name, e.department_id AS department FROM employees e;

title: Name the gap
prompt: Show each employee's name and department as department, using the text Unassigned for employees with no department.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT e.name, COALESCE(d.name, 'Unassigned') AS department FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id;
SELECT e.name, COALESCE(d.name, 'Unassigned') AS department FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id;

title: Department report
prompt: Show every department's name as department, its staff count as staff, and its total salary as total_salary, with 0 for empty departments. Sort by department.
hints: Count and sum from the right table, with COALESCE.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(e.id) AS staff, COALESCE(SUM(e.salary), 0) AS total_salary FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.name ORDER BY department;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(*) AS staff, COALESCE(SUM(e.salary), 0) AS total_salary FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.name ORDER BY department;
SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(e.id) AS staff, SUM(e.salary) AS total_salary FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.name ORDER BY department;
